study.title: Determining the Precise Cerebral Response to Acupuncture: An Improved fMRI Study
study.study_design: 2×2 randomized, controlled, participant-blinded cross-over factorial acupuncture trial
study.randomization: All the subjects were divided into four groups randomly.
study.population: Forty-one college students with myopia (male/female = 21/20, age 25.7±3.7 years, all right-handed)
study.inclusion_criteria: college students with myopia, right-handed, no history of neurological or psychiatric illness, acupuncture naive, free of any transient medical problems, did not take any medications the day prior to the study
study.exclusion_criteria: history of neurological or psychiatric illness; not acupuncture naive; transient medical problems; medications taken the day prior to the study

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle inserted approximately 10 mm into a sham acupoint, which exceeds the 5 mm threshold for full penetration. At this depth the needle reaches muscle/fascia, activating deep mechanoreceptors. The sham nature is based on location (non-acupoint), not depth.

conditions.condition_label_exact: sham acupuncture (SA) with non-treatment instruction (NI) — Group D
conditions.scan_context: fMRI during manual needle twirling at sham acupoint; participant told they were in experiment to estimate medical machine sensitivity of detecting tactile signals
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Identical physical procedure to cond_sham_C: needle inserted approximately 10 mm into the same sham acupoint location, exceeding the 5 mm threshold. Full tissue penetration into muscle/fascia with deep mechanoreceptor activation. The only difference from cond_sham_C is the verbal instruction given to the participant, which does not affect physical depth of tissue engagement.

extraction_notes.note: The paper states that data were normalized to MNI space but reports coordinates in Talairach space. This is a potential inconsistency. It is unclear whether conversion between MNI and Talairach space was performed. All coordinates are extracted as reported (stated to be Talairach) but this discrepancy should be noted for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The paper describes the design as '262 cross-over factorial' in the abstract but states each subject underwent only one of the four interventions (no cross-over). The design appears to be a parallel-group 2×2 factorial trial, not a cross-over. This is an internal inconsistency in the paper.
Individual credibility score means/SDs for Groups A and C are not reported in the text or tables; only the chi-square p-values (QB: p=0.42; QA: p=0.56) are provided.

The specific statistical test and p-value for the comparison of needle sensation scores between RA and SA groups are not explicitly reported; only the directional statement 'RA did elicit significantly different sensations from SA' is provided.
No adverse events are reported or mentioned in the paper.

The exact neuroimaging scan duration for the post-needle-extraction phase is not explicitly stated; the paper says scanning continued 'for a total of 402 scans for every subject' with first 2 scans discarded leaving 400 volumes. The stimulation phase was 60 scans and resting phase was 62 scans (first 2 discarded), leaving the remaining scans unspecified for the post-extraction period.

The label 'VI' appears in the Group A vs. Group B contrast table (row: R, 20 −82 −11, Z=3.57) but is not included in the table footnote abbreviations. It likely refers to primary visual cortex (V1) or a cerebellar lobule VI, but this is ambiguous and has been extracted verbatim as 'VI'.
The fMRI analysis used a box-car response function convolved with a Poisson hemodynamic response function, which is non-standard. The exact parameterization of the Poisson HRF is not described.

The paper reports both a 'combined' RA group (Groups A+B) and a 'combined' SA group (Groups C+D) for the primary RA vs. SA contrast, and also a combined EG (Groups A+C) vs. NE (Groups B+D) comparison. These groupings are used for specific contrasts; arm composition for each contrast has been noted in the contrast entries.
Cluster sizes (in voxels or mm³) are not reported for any contrast. Only Z-statistics and Talairach coordinates are given.

The paper does not report between-group comparisons for needle sensation scores with explicit test statistics or p-values despite stating significance. Specific NSQ subscale data are also not provided; only total scores are reported.

The sham acupuncture in this study uses an actual penetrating needle at a non-classical location (10 mm anterior to LR3), with the same depth and manipulation as real acupuncture. This is a 'sham acupoint' design, not a retractable/non-penetrating sham needle. The sham thus involves genuine needle penetration and twirling, which may produce physiological effects.
Head motion exclusion criteria and motion parameters are not explicitly stated beyond 'after realignment'.
